source_review.notes: Checked current Linux KVM, QEMU, Xen, Microsoft Hyper-V and Firecracker documentation for kernel/userspace splits, locking, vCPU requests, device processes, security boundaries, service domains, root partitions and per-VM VMMs. All ten cited URLs returned HTTP 200 after normal redirects; deployed architectures, design documents, abstract models and assurance claims remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked component, authority-edge, reachable-resource, blast-radius, service, queue, crossing, arrival-rate, parallelism and lifecycle-generation notation.
Reviewed transitive authority, serial path latency, shared-component utilization and generation-fenced mutation relations.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation separates authority reachability from exploitability, service from waiting and lifecycle identity from component process identity.

evidence: Executed transitive resource reachability for per-VM VMM, shared backend and control-plane components.
Confirmed each printed leaf set; independently recomputed serial latency as 52 microseconds and two-worker nominal backend utilization as 0.72.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic computation validates one toy authority graph only; it establishes no exploitability, deployed permissions, complete TCB, containment or security property.

evidence: Re-derived compromise blast radius as reachable resource union and serial request latency as service, queue and crossing sums.
Checked shared-service utilization and lifecycle mutation guarded by current generation plus fencing authority.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations are architecture reasoning tools and do not claim a complete formalization of hypervisors, kernels, schedulers, IPC, migration or adversaries.

evidence: Reviewed ambient privilege, shared credentials, stale vCPU requests, split interrupt state, malformed IPC, shared-memory revocation and control-plane split ownership.
Reviewed exit storms, backend saturation, restart during writes, device assignment teardown, mixed-version migration, service-domain failure and residual hardware coupling.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Authority, state, scheduling, device, IPC, lifecycle, recovery, compatibility, migration and assurance boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced CPU, memory, interrupt, device, policy and lifecycle responsibilities through bare-metal, hosted, root-partition and per-VM-process organizations.
Verified least authority, privileged-effect validation, single-generation ownership, tenant identity, fencing, restart semantics and compatible upgrades.
invariant_checking.notes: The chapter treats kernels, hypervisors, service domains, VMMs, backends and control planes as a connected authority and failure graph rather than one label.

evidence: Reviewed the responsibility map, authority overlay, data flow, single ownership, validation, component-removal and recovery argument.
Constructed counterexamples for type-one-as-small-TCB, process-count-as-security, separate-backend-as-isolation, local-socket-as-trust and boot-test-as-containment.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies reusable architecture obligations, not a formal proof of KVM, QEMU, Xen, Hyper-V, Firecracker, a deployment or a threat model.

evidence: Audited uses of bare-metal, hosted, minimal, trusted, isolated, contained, authoritative, fenced, restartable and compatible.
Confirmed vendor architecture, design intent, abstract graph, operational recommendations, examples and assurance limits remain separately scoped.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: Bare-metal is not labeled a small TCB, process separation is not labeled containment, reachability is not labeled exploitation and confidential execution is not labeled removal of every host dependency.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/OS-083/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, toolchain and environment for authority reachability.
Reviewed required deployed version, credential, namespace, policy, descriptor, mapping, service-domain, device, lifecycle and fault-injection evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes three graph traversals only; it provides no evidence for real permissions, process confinement, hypervisor isolation, backend recovery, performance or security.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed hypervisor architecture as explicit placement of responsibility, authority, state and failure containment across privileged cores, domains, kernels, VMMs, backends and control planes.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including vCPU loops, scheduler composition, memory mappings, interrupt ownership, device backends, IPC, lifecycle generations, confinement, restart, observability, upgrades and migration. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from responsibility inventory and topology comparisons through vCPU, memory, interrupt, device, control-plane, authority, failure, upgrade and migration analysis, followed by twelve obligations, sixteen trade-offs, twenty-five misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external operating-systems academic, hypervisor or VMM maintainer, platform architect, security reviewer, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
